need: stop the accounts payable team from paying fake requests
clues: an email from the real CEO's account asked for an urgent wire transfer to a new account
a supplier's usual contact emailed new bank details for all future invoices
the messages came from legitimate company and supplier mailboxes
appliesWhen: attackers use compromised or impersonated business email accounts to redirect payments
explanation: Business email compromise uses a real or impersonated business mailbox to trick staff into sending money, often by changing bank details on invoices. Training teaches staff to verify payment changes through a known phone number before acting.
source: CompTIA Security+ SY0-701 Cert Guide (Heuermann) – Chapter 6: Understanding Common Threat Vectors and Attack Surfaces; CompTIA Security+ SY0-701 Certification Guide, 3rd edition (Neil) – Chapter 6: Explain common threat vectors and attack surfaces

need: protect company email that staff read on their own phones
clues: many personal phones have no screen lock
staff save work attachments to personal apps on the same phones
the company allows employees to use their own devices for work
appliesWhen: employees use personal devices for company work and data
explanation: When staff use their own devices for work, company data mixes with personal data on devices the company does not fully control. Training covers screen locks, updates, and keeping work data in approved apps.
source: CompTIA Security+ SY0-701 Certification Guide, 3rd edition (Neil) – Chapter 28: Given a scenario, implement security awareness practices

need: respond to an employee who entered his password on a simulated phishing page
clues: he is one of only three employees who failed this month's test
the goal is to fix his behavior, not to punish him
he completed the yearly course two months ago
appliesWhen: one person made a specific mistake and needs follow-up training to correct it
explanation: Employees who fall for a simulated phishing attack are retrained so they learn from the mistake. Phishing results should guide learning and should not be used to punish or call out employees.
source: CompTIA Security+ SY0-701 Certification Guide, 3rd edition (Neil) – Chapter 28: Given a scenario, implement security awareness practices; NIST SP 800-50 Rev. 1, Building a Cybersecurity and Privacy Learning Program (sections 2.4 and 2.7); Microsoft Learn – Get started using Attack simulation training

need: brief staff about a new attack technique that the sector's threat-sharing group reported last week
clues: the technique did not exist when this year's course was written
attackers are already using it against similar companies
the regular modules do not mention it
appliesWhen: a new threat has appeared that the existing training does not cover
explanation: Training goals must match the organization's current needs, which can mean covering newly emerging attacks instead of the usual topics. The program should be updated as threats evolve.
source: CompTIA Security+ SY0-701 Certification Guide, 3rd edition (Neil) – Chapter 28: Given a scenario, implement security awareness practices; CompTIA Security+ SY0-701 Cert Guide (Heuermann) – Chapter 28: Implementing Security Awareness Practices

need: learn what employees thought of a new training course so it can be improved
clues: the team wants to know whether the course was clear and met its goals
participants should answer in their own words in a free-text box
the answers will be used to change the course content and delivery
appliesWhen: the team needs participants' opinions of a course to find gaps in its content or delivery
explanation: After a course, participants evaluate it in a survey or questionnaire. Their feedback shows weak points in the content or delivery so the training team can improve the program.
source: CompTIA Security+ SY0-701 Certification Guide, 3rd edition (Neil) – Chapter 28: Given a scenario, implement security awareness practices

need: deliver required security courses to 4,000 staff at 12 sites and prove who finished them
clues: auditors want completion records for every employee
courses must be assigned to staff by role and tracked to completion
staff take the courses online at different times
appliesWhen: training must be assigned, delivered online, and tracked with completion records for many people
explanation: A learning management system delivers course content, registers participants, and keeps course completion records. It lets the organization assign training at scale and prove completion to auditors.
source: NIST SP 800-50 Rev. 1, Building a Cybersecurity and Privacy Learning Program (sections 2.4 and 2.7); PhishingBox – Dedicated training portal (learning management system)

need: keep senior leadership informed each quarter about the awareness program
clues: leaders want completion rates and incident trends for each department
the summary must be short and need no technical knowledge
it is reviewed at the quarterly management meeting

answer.item: A managerial report of program results

appliesWhen: leadership needs a periodic summary of program results and trends
explanation: Recurring reports are generated weekly, monthly, or quarterly and include metrics such as incidents detected and training completion. Managerial reports present these results to leadership so it can make decisions about the program.
source: CompTIA Security+ SY0-701 Cert Guide (Heuermann) – Chapter 28: Implementing Security Awareness Practices; CompTIA Security+ SY0-701 Certification Guide, 3rd edition (Neil) – Chapter 28: Given a scenario, implement security awareness practices

need: find out whether the new phishing training is actually working
clues: the team ran a simulated phishing test before the training and will run another after it
the measures must be numbers that can be compared over time
the results should show both clicks and reports of the test email

answer.item: Metrics such as phishing click and report rates

appliesWhen: the team must measure the effect of training with comparable numbers
explanation: Metrics such as click rates, report rates, and incident counts turn the program's effect into numbers. Comparing them before and after training shows whether behavior changed.
source: CompTIA Security+ Practice Tests: Exam SY0-701 (Seidl) – Chapter 5: Domain 5.0: Security Program Management and Oversight; CompTIA Security+ SY0-701 Certification Guide, 3rd edition (Neil) – Chapter 28: Given a scenario, implement security awareness practices

need: prepare 20 new hires who start on Monday to work safely
clues: the new staff have not yet received their accounts
they must learn the acceptable use policy and password rules before they get access
they have never had any security training at this company
appliesWhen: new staff must learn the security rules before they receive access
explanation: Initial training is part of onboarding, along with orientation and account creation. It teaches new staff the security policies and expected behavior before they use company systems.
source: CompTIA Security+ Practice Tests: Exam SY0-701 (Seidl) – Chapter 5: Domain 5.0: Security Program Management and Oversight; CompTIA Security+ SY0-701 Cert Guide (Heuermann) – Chapter 28: Implementing Security Awareness Practices

need: explain a new remote work policy to all 600 employees at the same time
clues: every employee must hear the same message on the same day
the CISO wants to take live questions from the audience
the session will be held as a company-wide webinar
appliesWhen: one message must reach a large audience at the same time
explanation: One-to-many delivery, such as a classroom lecture or a virtual session, lets one presenter reach many people at once with the same message. It is efficient for announcements that everyone must hear.
source: CompTIA Security+ SY0-701 Certification Guide, 3rd edition (Neil) – Chapter 28: Given a scenario, implement security awareness practices; NIST SP 800-50 Rev. 1, Building a Cybersecurity and Privacy Learning Program (sections 2.4 and 2.7); risk3sixty – Annual Security Training, Phase 3: Deliver

need: help a senior executive who keeps falling for impersonation attempts
clues: the executive has failed several tests in a row
the mistakes are specific to how she handles requests from her assistants
she wants a private session that fits her schedule and her questions
appliesWhen: a single person needs personal, interactive instruction that fits their situation
explanation: One-to-one training is interactive instruction, coaching, or mentoring for a single person. It lets the trainer focus on that person's specific mistakes and questions, which a group session cannot do.
source: NIST SP 800-50 Rev. 1, Building a Cybersecurity and Privacy Learning Program (sections 2.4 and 2.7); CyberAware – How to design an escalation path for repeat phishing clickers

need: keep staff alert to phishing after the first round of training
clues: phishing incidents dropped after last year's course but are rising again six months later
users seem to have become complacent
the whole workforce is affected, not one team
appliesWhen: knowledge fades over time and the whole workforce needs regular refreshers
explanation: Awareness fades, and users become complacent months after training. Recurring training on a regular schedule reeducates the whole workforce and keeps awareness current.
source: CompTIA Security+ SY0-701 Certification Guide, 3rd edition (Neil) – Chapter 28: Given a scenario, implement security awareness practices; CompTIA Security+ SY0-701 Cert Guide (Heuermann) – Chapter 28: Implementing Security Awareness Practices

need: stop staff from revealing internal details in daily work and online
clues: an employee posted a photo of a whiteboard with network diagrams on social media
staff discuss unreleased projects in public places
confidential printouts are left on desks overnight
appliesWhen: staff reveal sensitive details through everyday habits, posts, or conversations
explanation: Operational security protects sensitive information in day-to-day activity, including what staff share in posts, conversations, and printouts. Practices such as a clean desk policy and care with what is shared reduce leaks.
source: CompTIA Security+ SY0-701 Cert Guide (Heuermann) – Chapter 28: Implementing Security Awareness Practices; CompTIA Security+ Practice Tests: Exam SY0-701 (Seidl) – Chapter 5: Domain 5.0: Security Program Management and Oversight

need: reduce the risk from the way staff choose and store their passwords
clues: an audit found the same password used on work and personal sites
several users keep passwords on sticky notes
many accounts still lack a second factor
appliesWhen: users reuse, write down, or weakly protect their passwords and credentials
explanation: Password training covers strong, unique passwords for each service, the risk of reuse, password managers, and enabling multifactor authentication. Audits then check that staff follow the policy.
source: CompTIA Security+ SY0-701 Cert Guide (Heuermann) – Chapter 28: Implementing Security Awareness Practices; CompTIA Security+ Practice Tests: Exam SY0-701 (Seidl) – Chapter 5: Domain 5.0: Security Program Management and Oversight

task: building a new security awareness training course

steps.do: Define the goals and needs the course must meet
steps.done: defined the goals and needs the course must meet

explanation: An awareness course starts with its goals and needs, which decide the material that is developed and how it is delivered. Feedback and monitoring of completion and results come after delivery and feed back into the next round of goals.
source: CompTIA Security+ SY0-701 Certification Guide, 3rd edition (Neil) – Chapter 28: Given a scenario, implement security awareness practices

need: secure staff who now work from home and from cafes three days a week
clues: employees connect from coffee shop Wi-Fi
home routers still use their default passwords
some staff do not start the VPN before they work
appliesWhen: staff work outside the office on home or public networks
explanation: Remote and hybrid work brings risks such as weak home networks and public Wi-Fi. Training covers securing the home router, keeping devices patched, avoiding public Wi-Fi, and always using the VPN.
source: CompTIA Security+ SY0-701 Cert Guide (Heuermann) – Chapter 28: Implementing Security Awareness Practices; CompTIA Security+ SY0-701 Certification Guide, 3rd edition (Neil) – Chapter 28: Given a scenario, implement security awareness practices

need: deal with USB devices that keep turning up around the building
clues: several flash drives labeled 'Salaries' were found in the parking lot
a charging cable arrived in the mail from an unknown sender
an employee plugged in a found drive to see who owned it
appliesWhen: unknown USB drives, cables, or other removable devices may carry malware or leak data
explanation: Removable media and cables can carry malware or be used to steal data. Training teaches users never to connect unknown drives or cables and to hand found devices to IT.
source: CompTIA Security+ SY0-701 Certification Guide, 3rd edition (Neil) – Chapter 28: Given a scenario, implement security awareness practices; CompTIA Security+ SY0-701 Cert Guide (Heuermann) – Chapter 28: Implementing Security Awareness Practices

task: responding to a suspicious email that an employee reported

steps.do: Quarantine the email so no one else can interact with it
Analyze the message for phishing indicators
steps.done: analyzed the message for phishing indicators

steps.do: Inform the reporting user and other staff about the attempt
steps.done: informed the reporting user and other staff about the attempt

steps.do: Update email filters and training based on the findings
steps.done: updated the email filters and training

explanation: A reported message is isolated first so no one else clicks it, then analyzed and passed to IT security. Users are then told about the attempt, and filters and training are updated to stop similar attacks.
source: CompTIA Security+ SY0-701 Cert Guide (Heuermann) – Chapter 28: Implementing Security Awareness Practices

need: find which individual employees pose the most human risk so they get attention first
clues: the team combines each person's phishing test results, overdue training, and risky actions
each employee should get a value that can be ranked
the result decides who gets extra coaching first
appliesWhen: individual people must be ranked by the risk their behavior creates
explanation: Behavior risk scoring gives each person a score from data such as simulated phishing actions, training completion, and other risky behavior. The scores rank people so the program can focus help where the risk is highest.
source: Keepnet Labs documentation – Executive Reports (Users with Highest Risk Scores); Abnormal AI – The formula behind Abnormal’s phishing risk score; NIST SP 800-50 Rev. 1, Building a Cybersecurity and Privacy Learning Program (sections 2.4 and 2.7)

need: give employees a place where they can get security help whenever they need it
clues: staff want to look up the latest policies and tips on their own
they want short how-to guides and a way to report a suspicious message
no trainer is needed for each visit
appliesWhen: people need on-demand access to guides, policies, and reporting tools without a trainer
explanation: A self-service portal is one place where users find security guides, tips, policies, training, and a way to report suspicious messages on their own schedule. It supports learning on demand without a trainer.
source: NIST SP 800-50 Rev. 1, Building a Cybersecurity and Privacy Learning Program (sections 2.4 and 2.7); University of Toronto Information Security – Cyber security awareness resources; PhishingBox – Dedicated training portal

need: make staff notice people and events around them that could be a threat
clues: a stranger followed employees through the secure door twice this week
someone was seen watching a nurse type her password at a shared station
the team wants staff to notice and report odd behavior
appliesWhen: staff must watch their surroundings and the behavior of people around them
explanation: Situational awareness means watching the environment and the behavior of people nearby, understanding what could go wrong, and reporting it. It helps staff spot threats such as tailgating and shoulder surfing.
source: CompTIA Security+ Practice Tests: Exam SY0-701 (Seidl) – Chapter 5: Domain 5.0: Security Program Management and Oversight; CompTIA Security+ SY0-701 Certification Guide, 3rd edition (Neil) – Chapter 28: Given a scenario, implement security awareness practices

need: prepare staff for callers and text messages that pretend to come from the help desk
clues: several employees were asked for their passwords by someone claiming to be IT
one employee got a text urging her to confirm her login details at once
the attackers rely on urgency and pretending to have authority
appliesWhen: people are being manipulated by pretexting, vishing, smishing, or similar tricks
explanation: Social engineering exploits human psychology, such as urgency and authority, to get access or information. Training with real examples and simulations teaches staff to recognize these tricks and verify requests through official channels.
source: CompTIA Security+ SY0-701 Cert Guide (Heuermann) – Chapter 28: Implementing Security Awareness Practices; CompTIA Security+ SY0-701 Certification Guide, 3rd edition (Neil) – Chapter 28: Given a scenario, implement security awareness practices

need: reduce the risk to the finance team, which attackers keep singling out
clues: phishing tests show the finance team clicks far more often than other departments
the attacks aimed at them ask for urgent payments to new accounts
the rest of the company already does well in the same tests

answer.item: Targeted training for the finance team

appliesWhen: one group or role faces particular threats or shows weak results and needs content made for it
explanation: Targeted, role-based training gives a group content that fits its duties and the threats aimed at it. Click rates by group show which teams need more targeted training.
source: CompTIA Security+ SY0-701 Certification Guide, 3rd edition (Neil) – Chapter 28: Given a scenario, implement security awareness practices; NIST SP 800-50 Rev. 1, Building a Cybersecurity and Privacy Learning Program (sections 2.4 and 2.7); Microsoft Learn – Get started using Attack simulation training
